checks.area: sign table vs decisions and physics
checks.evidence: Derived independently with x right, y up and z = x × y out of the page, which is the person's right when they face +x (right = forward × up). Viewed from +z, counterclockwise rotates +x toward +y. Thigh: down (0,-1) toward +x is CCW, so knee forward/hip flexion is +. Shank relative to thigh rotating backward (knee flexion) is CW, so flexion is − and extension +. Foot forward (1,0) toward +y is CCW, so toes up/dorsiflexion is +. PSIS→ASIS line (1,0) with the front dropping is CW, so anterior tilt is − and posterior +. Trunk up (0,1) with the shoulders moving back toward -x is CCW, so leaning back is +. Internal moments: knee extensor +, knee flexor −, ankle plantarflexor −, hip flexor +, each consistent with its angle. Power M·ω is invariant to the shared sign flip, so generation is +. Callout values: 60° flexion = −1.047 rad, stated −1.05. gait2392 equivalents are correct. hip_flexion is flexion +. knee_angle is flexion −: the model knee range in gt21-c01-conventions.json is [−2.0944, 0.1745] rad. ankle_angle is dorsiflexion +. pelvis_tilt is posterior +. lumbar_extension is about z, extension +, per the same audit's model axes. The ID output name knee_angle_r_moment is correct. Segment rows are labelled '(same sense)', not as equalities, which is correct. Sideways GRF/CoP is +z for the right leg and −z for the left, matching B. GRF forward + and braking − agree with the existing default_ranges.yaml (grf_anterior_ipsi negative early in stance).

Every arc uses sweep-flag 0 (visually counterclockwise in SVG's y-down space) with the arrowhead at the arc end. I checked each arc against its centre and limb vector. Hip starts on the thigh axis and rotates forward. Knee starts on the shank axis and rotates forward (extension). Thigh and shank start on dashed verticals. Foot starts at the heel-to-toe line and rotates up. Ankle rotates toes-up toward the shank. Pelvis rises at the front. Trunk rotates back. The head's nose points +x. Axes: +x right, +y up, +z drawn as a dot in a circle (out of page). Labels match the table. Rendered from a local copy with headless Chrome at 390 px and 1100 px: the diagram is legible at phone width (about 14 px text) and readable in about 5 seconds. The 390 px page has horizontal overflow (scrollWidth 485), which also occurs on the HEAD version, so it is pre-existing and not caused by this task. Cosmetic, non-blocking: the trunk arc starts about 10° behind vertical rather than at the trunk axis, and the callout text uses the muted grey of the existing callout style.

Each added claim is physically consistent, but none is marked as a LocoHub definition separate from the decisions. In DATA_CONTRACT.md, the line 'Summary, adopted 2026-10-30 (decisions D-UM21-C03-1 = C and D-GT21-C01-1 = B)' is followed by the GRF-on-the-person bullet, so the reader takes it as decided. The reference page also states every row as 'adopted'. (a) GRF acting on the person: consistent with existing ranges and the GT21 audit, and low risk. (b) Segment zero references (thigh/shank from straight down; foot and pelvis PSIS→ASIS from forward horizontal): these come from the UM21-C03 audit 'derivations', not from the decision text. The trunk zero is undefined. (c) The 'Joint angles' bullet says 'signs compose: thigh = pelvis + hip, shank = thigh + knee, foot = shank + ankle' as exact equalities. The same bullet then says joint zero references (e.g. static-pose subtraction) are dataset-specific, so the equalities hold only up to constant offsets. The table also gives segment zeros as fixed. A reader could compute shank = thigh + knee and expect an exact match. (d) Trunk leaning back + follows directly from 'counterclockwise for everything' and is fine. (e) The CoP origin is correctly left dataset-specific.
